meta.name: Speicherstadt Queues (Even Rotation)
meta.blurb: Twelve rounds of secret worker queues on three goods lots, bought through a falling-price offer in a rotating priority order, chasing a hidden contract colour.

rules:
There are {colours} colours: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Purple, Orange. The deck has {deck_size} cards, {cards_per_colour} of each colour, shuffled once at the start. Each player is privately dealt a different contract colour, drawn at random from the 6 without repetition. No one else learns it. Each player starts with {starting_coins} coins and no goods. Players are numbered 1 to N (N = 3 or 4) in seating order.

The game lasts exactly {rounds} rounds. Each round:
1. SUPPLY: Reveal the top {lots_per_round} cards of the deck as Lot 1, Lot 2 and Lot 3. Each lot is one good of the card's colour.
2. INCOME: Every player gains {income_per_round} coins.
3. PRIORITY: This round's priority order starts with player ((round - 1) mod N) + 1 and continues in seat order, wrapping around from N back to 1. It is announced. Over the 12 rounds every player holds each position in the priority order exactly 12/N times.
4. TALK: Everyone writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others. All messages are then shown to everyone. Messages are not binding and may be false.
5. QUEUE (secret, simultaneous): Each player submits three whole numbers, one per lot, each from {limit_min} to {limit_max}. A 0 means no worker on that lot. A positive number places a worker there, and that number is the highest price the player will pay for that lot. Each player has {workers_per_player} workers, so at most 2 of the 3 numbers may be positive. If more than 2 are positive, only the positive entries on the two lowest-numbered lots count, and the rest become 0 (if your Lot 1 and Lot 2 limits are both positive, you are not asked for Lot 3 and your Lot 3 limit is 0).
6. RESOLVE Lot 1, then Lot 2, then Lot 3: The queue for a lot is every player with a positive number on it, ordered by this round's priority order. Let k be the queue length. The offer starts at price k and goes to the first player in the queue. If that player's limit is at least the current price and they hold at least that many coins, they pay that many coins to the bank and take the good. Otherwise they decline, the price drops by {price_drop_per_decline}, and the offer passes to the next player in the queue. The k-th player is therefore offered price {lowest_offer_price}. If nobody buys, the card is discarded. A lot with an empty queue is discarded. Coins spent on an earlier lot this round count when checking later lots.
7. ANNOUNCE: For each lot, announce which players queued, who bought it (if anyone) and the price paid. Limits are never revealed. Every player's coins and goods held (with colours) are public at all times.
8. END CHECK: After round {rounds} the deck is empty and the game ends.

FINAL SCORING: Each player's score is their coins, plus {contract_good_points} points for each good of their own contract colour, plus {other_good_points} points for each good of any other colour. All contract colours are then revealed.

The player with the highest final score wins. If several tie for highest, the tied player with more goods of their own contract colour wins. If they are still tied, they share the win as a draw.
